NMF of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) composition in the GSE243013 NSCLC anti-PD1 single-cell atlas (1,254,749 cells; 243 patients; 51 annotated immune cell subtypes) identifies an OPTIMAL CLASSIFICATION AT k = 4 PROGRAMS.

METHOD (summary)
- Built a 243 x 51 patient x cell-type composition matrix (percentage of each patient's immune cells per subtype), variance-stabilized with the arcsine-square-root transform (Y = 100*arcsin(sqrt(p)); non-negative as required by NMF).
- NMF (scikit-learn, NNDSVDa init, Frobenius/coordinate-descent, max_iter 1000, tol 1e-5); rank scan k = 2..8 with 100 restarts per rank; consensus matrices scored by cophenetic correlation (Brunet 2004) and dispersion (Kim & Park 2007); rank additionally judged by reconstruction-error elbow, 10%-masked cross-validated held-out error, program sizes, and clinical association.

WHY k = 4
- Consensus stability is near-perfect for all k <= 7 (dispersion 1.000 for k = 2..6, 0.9995 at k = 7; first instability at k = 8 with dispersion 0.83), so stability alone cannot pick k.
- Reconstruction error falls monotonically; the last double-digit relative gain is 2->3 (-15.7%) and 3->4 (-11.3%), then ~7% per factor (elbow after k = 4).
- Cross-validated held-out error has its optimum at k = 3-4 (RMSE 5.70 at k = 3, 5.88 at k = 4 vs 6.47 at k = 2 and 6.85 at k = 7).
- k = 4 has no singleton programs (sizes 4/31/100/108) and gives by far the strongest association with pathological response of any rank tested (chi-square p = 1.6e-08 vs p = 0.17 at k = 3 and p = 4.0e-03 at k = 5).

THE FOUR PATIENT CLASSES (n = 243)
- C1 Myeloid-rich (n = 4): MARCO+/VCAN+/FOLR2+ macrophages and cDC2 dominate; T/NK compartment compressed.
- C2 B-cell-rich (n = 31): naive/memory B (Bm_PDE4D, Bm_TNFSF9, Bm_CD74), plasma cells, germinal-center B (GCB_RGS13) - a B/TLS-like infiltrate.
- C3 Treg/exhausted-T (n = 100): expanded FOXP3+ Tregs (7.0% of all cells) and CCR8+ Tregs (3.8%), CXCL13+ and LAYN+ exhausted CD8 T cells.
- C4 NK/cytotoxic (n = 108): CD16hi FGFBP2+ NK cells (5.4%), CD8+ NK-like cells (4.0%), GZMK+ effector-memory and IL7R+ memory CD8 T cells, few Tregs (2.9%).

CLINICAL VALIDATION (pathological response, n = 242; 1 unlabeled patient excluded)
- 3-level response (non-MPR/MPR/pCR) x class: chi-square = 47.35, dof = 6, p = 1.6e-08.
- Responder rates (MPR + pCR vs non-MPR): C1 0/4 (0%); C2 22/31 (71.0%, OR 2.33, 95% CI 1.03-5.30); C3 30/99 (30.3%, OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.19-0.54, Fisher p = 1.1e-09); C4 78/108 (72.2%, OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.38-7.08, Fisher p = 2.0e-07). Overall responder rate 130/242 (53.7%).
- Continuous loadings show the same dose-response: P3 loading vs responder Spearman rho = -0.37 (p = 2.2e-09); P4 rho = +0.41 (p = 4.1e-11); Mann-Whitney p = 1e-33 to 1e-36.
- Robust to histology: effect holds separately in LUAD (C3 7% vs C4 57% responders, p = 1.5e-04) and LUSC (C3 39% vs C4 76%, p = 1.4e-05), and in regression adjusted for histology (P3 beta = -0.54, p = 1e-04; P4 beta = +0.34, p = 7e-04; LUSC beta = -0.23, p = 6e-04).
- No confounding by cells sampled per patient (rho = -0.07, p = 0.26), age, gender, smoking history, stage, treatment cycles, or radiological response (all p > 0.2).
- Replicated on raw percentages without the transform (p = 1.7e-05 at k = 4); the P3/P4 axis is recovered within responders only (k = 2 NMF inside the 142 MPR/pCR patients correlates r = 0.795 with P4), ruling out a response/cell-count artifact.

BIOLOGICAL INTERPRETATION
The optimal NMF classification is a parts-based, lineage-archetype partition of the TIME along two axes: an immune-cold myeloid-suppressive pole (C1, MARCO+ macrophage-dominated) and, within lymphocyte-rich tumors, a T-cell-state pole separating Treg-enriched, terminally exhausted (CXCL13+/LAYN+) infiltrates (C3) from NK/cytotoxic effector-rich infiltrates (C4), with a B-cell/TLS-like class (C2) in between. The 2.4-fold responder-rate gap between C4 (72%) and C3 (30%) is consistent with Treg-mediated suppression and T-cell dysfunction opposing the NK/cytotoxic effector program that anti-PD1 therapy acts on, and the B-rich class aligns with tertiary-lymphoid-structure/B-cell predictors of checkpoint response.

ANSWER IN ONE LINE
The optimal NMF-based patient classification of this NSCLC anti-PD1 cohort uses k = 4 tumor immune microenvironment programs - myeloid-rich (n = 4), B-cell-rich (n = 31), Treg/exhausted-CD8-rich (n = 100), and NK/cytotoxic-effector-rich (n = 108) - and the resulting classes predict pathological response (chi-square p = 1.6e-08): NK/cytotoxic-rich patients respond at 72% while Treg/exhausted-rich patients respond at 30% (OR 4.1 vs 0.32), an effect that persists within LUAD and LUSC and after adjustment for histology.

MAIN LIMITATIONS
Analysis uses provided cell-level annotations (composition-level, no expression re-analysis); stability diagnostics saturate so k = 4 rests on elbow + cross-validation + interpretability + external association rather than a stability optimum (cross-validated minimum is technically k = 3); C1 is small (n = 4); histology, regimen composition, and other residual confounders are reduced but not eliminated; the design is observational and pre-treatment, so the class-response link is predictive, not causal.
grader_notes: The analysis is strong overall, with a principled NMF workflow, robust stability assessment, dual justification for k=4, and thorough clinical interpretation; the main deductions are lack of cell-count filter and a single-initialisation final model.

QUESTIONS
Using the provided self-assembling, partner-dependent, non-phase-separating protein sets (SaPS, PdPS, and NoPS) and the human proteome (hSaPS, hPdPS, hNoPS), compare amino-acid composition differences between PS-Self and PS-Part proteins, and evaluate the performance of four phase-separation predictors (PScore, PLAAC, catGRANULE, and FuzDrop) in distinguishing each PS type from non-PS proteins.

DATA
sequence_prediction_filtered.xlsx: 48,504 proteins x 23 columns (sequences, predictor scores, SaPS/hSaPS/PdPS/hPdPS/NoPS/hNoPS labels). Set sizes: SaPS 128, hSaPS 59, PdPS 214, hPdPS 96, NoPS 48,158, hNoPS 8,801; sets are disjoint. FuzDrop is NOT present in the file (verified by raw XML scan), so only PScore, PLAAC and catGRANULE could be evaluated; FuzDrop = unavailable.

1) AMINO-ACID COMPOSITION: PS-SELF (SaPS) VS PS-PART (PdPS)
Two-sided Mann-Whitney U per residue, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR; effect size as rank-biserial AUC (P(SaPS > PdPS)).

Benchmark sets (128 vs 214) — 13 of 20 residues differ at q < 0.05:
- HIGHER in SaPS (PS-Self): G +2.86 pp (mean 9.37% vs 6.52%; AUC 0.70, q = 5e-12), P +1.29 pp (7.38% vs 6.09%; AUC 0.60, q = 0.003), Q +0.79 pp (AUC 0.60, q = 0.005), S +0.96 pp (AUC 0.59, q = 0.008); Q+N combined AUC 0.60.
- LOWER in SaPS (i.e. higher in PdPS/PS-Part): L −1.62 pp (7.01% vs 8.63%; AUC 0.32, q = 2e-12), K −1.31 pp (5.48% vs 6.80%; AUC 0.36, q = 1e-4), E −1.13 pp (6.43% vs 7.56%; AUC 0.37, q = 1e-4), I −0.90 pp (AUC 0.35), D −0.72 pp (AUC 0.39), R −0.75 pp (AUC 0.43), V −0.46 pp (AUC 0.41), C −0.32 pp (AUC 0.39), H −0.33 pp (AUC 0.39).
- Net charge: FCR (D+E+K+R) is LOWER in SaPS, 22.2% vs 26.1% (AUC 0.33, q = 3e-6); NCPR does not differ significantly (AUC 0.54, q = 0.30) — SaPS proteins are less charged overall, not differently net-charged.
- Protein length does not differ (median 602 vs 565 aa, AUC 0.54, q = 0.25).
- Human subsets confirm the signature with smaller n (59 vs 96): G +2.55 pp (AUC 0.67, q = 0.005), E −1.37 pp (AUC 0.35, q = 0.009), K −1.42 pp (AUC 0.36, q = 0.013), L −1.62 pp (AUC 0.33, q = 0.005), FCR −4.2 pp (AUC 0.30, q = 4e-4); P and Q trend the same direction (AUC 0.59, q ≈ 0.18).

Interpretation: PS-Self proteins are enriched for the "low-complexity sticker-spacer" alphabet — glycine-rich, proline- and glutamine/asparagine-containing, with depleted hydrophobic/aliphatic bulk (L, I, V) and depleted charged residues (K, E, D, R) — consistent with self-association driven by multivalent weak interactions of prion-like/pliable low-complexity domains (e.g. FUS, hnRNPA1, TAF15). PS-Part (PdPS) proteins keep more conventional folded-domain chemistry (higher L/I/V hydrophobicity and higher K/E/D charge), consistent with phase separation that requires partners (RNA, SH3/PRM-type modules) rather than intrinsic self-adhesion of an IDR.

All three p-values for "score higher in PS class than NoPS" are < 1e-10 (one-sided Mann-Whitney). PR metrics are heavily class-imbalanced (NoPS base rates 0.3–1.1%): PR-AUC fold-over-random for SaPS tasks is 8–18x (e.g. PScore hSaPS PR-AUC 0.131 vs base 0.0073, 17.8x) but only ~2.5x for PdPS tasks; precision in the top 1% of the ranking reaches 5.1–22.7% for SaPS vs 1.9–8.8% for PdPS.

(c) Consequently the three general predictors also partially separate SaPS from PdPS (AUC 0.67–0.73), because they inherit the composition bias of self-assembling IDRs.
(d) The provided mechanism-aware 8/10-feature classifiers reach AUC 0.97–0.99 for their own mechanism vs NoPS and AUC ≈ 0.90–0.92 for SaPS vs PdPS, showing that composition-derived features carry the mechanistic signal; general PS predictors capture only the SaPS half of it.

Question: Can unsupervised clustering of hepatic transcriptomes (GSE135251, 206 NAFLD biopsies) stratify patients by disease severity for clinical-trial enrichment?

ANSWER: No. Unsupervised clustering of the hepatic transcriptomes does NOT stratify NAFLD patients by disease severity. The cohort contains a statistically robust binary molecular partition, but its clusters are clinically indistinguishable, and the dominant variance in the data is technical rather than biological.

WHAT WAS DONE
- Metadata from the GEO series matrix: 216 samples = 206 NAFLD cases (NAFL 51, NASH_F0-F1 34, NASH_F2 53, NASH_F3 54, NASH_F4 14) + 10 healthy controls; fibrosis stage 0-4, NAS 0-8, early (F0-F2, n=138) vs moderate (F3-F4, n=68); no missing values. Controls were excluded before clustering.
- Counts: 216 HTSeq files, 5 __-summary rows dropped per file -> 64,253 genes; filtered to 13,729 genes (CPM > 1 in >=30% of samples); TMM normalization (edgeR 4.0.16); log2-CPM (prior count 2).
- PCA + Ward hierarchical clustering on PC scores of the 206 NAFLD cases, k=2..8 assessed by mean silhouette, with sensitivity analyses (top-5,000-MAD genes, PC1-3, gene-scaled PCA, k up to 4, technical-covariate removal).

KEY RESULTS
1. The primary solution (all genes, PC1-2, Ward, k=2) splits the cohort 50 vs 156 with real structure: silhouette 0.472, cophenetic r=0.729, permutation test of silhouette p=0.0005, bootstrap within/between co-clustering 0.864/0.130, 0.71-0.94 agreement with alternative feature spaces.
2. But the clusters do NOT differ by any severity feature (chi-square / Fisher exact / Kruskal-Wallis / Spearman):
   - Fibrosis stage 0-4: chi2=3.88, dof=4, p=0.422 (medians 2 vs 2, p=0.725)
   - Advanced fibrosis F3-F4: 32.0% vs 33.3%, Fisher p=1.000
   - NAS score: medians 5 vs 5 (means 4.22 vs 4.61), Kruskal-Wallis p=0.225
   - NASH group (NAFL to NASH_F4): chi2=3.28, dof=4, p=0.512
   - Early vs moderate: 68.0% vs 66.7% early, chi2 p=0.999
   - All 28 tests across the sensitivity grid (feature spaces x PC number x k) were non-significant; smallest p anywhere = 0.178.
3. What the clusters actually track (exploratory): the file-name sequencing-batch proxy (chi2=12.06, p=0.0072; all 3 minority-site samples in the small cluster) and library size (Spearman rho=0.374, p<1e-7). PC1 correlates with library size (rho=-0.471, p=9.4e-13) but not fibrosis (rho=0.059) or NAS (rho=-0.078). As a positive control, re-clustering all 216 samples did not cleanly separate the 10 healthy controls from NAFLD cases either - further evidence that variance is dominated by technical factors.
4. Severity signal exists but is continuous, not discrete: after regressing out library size and batch, residual PC3 correlates strongly with fibrosis (rho=0.638, p=6.6e-25) and NAS (rho=0.467, p=1.6e-12), yet even there no Ward partition (k=2-4, 2-4 PCs) yields consistently significant severity-separated clusters (silhouettes <=0.36, non-replicating p~0.02-0.03).

INTERPRETATION AND IMPLICATION FOR TRIAL ENRICHMENT
Hepatic transcriptomic variation across the NAFLD spectrum in GSE135251 forms a stable binary partition driven by sequencing/processing characteristics, not histologic severity. Fibrosis stage and NAS are encoded in the residual transcriptome as a graded (continuous) signal consistent with the known continuous histologic progression of NAFLD, but they do not define discrete unsupervised molecular subtypes in this dataset. Unsupervised whole-transcriptome clustering is therefore NOT a usable enrichment/stratification tool here; trial enrichment should instead use histologic staging (e.g., F3-F4) or supervised transcriptomic classifiers built against the severity outcome.

MAIN LIMITATIONS
- GEO provides no explicit batch, sex, age, or BMI fields; the batch proxy derives from file-naming conventions, so residual site effects within the largest naming group cannot be excluded.
- Bulk-tissue signal may dilute severity-relevant cell-type changes; genes were analyzed by Ensembl ID without external annotation.
- Early/moderate and NASH-group labels are deterministic re-codings of fibrosis stage in this cohort, so their tests are not independent of the fibrosis test.
- Controls (n=10, healthy liver) are too few for the positive control to be definitive.

PIPELINE SUMMARY: 216 files -> 216 samples (206 NAFLD analyzed) -> 64,253 genes -> 13,729 after filtering -> TMM log2-CPM -> PCA (PC1 28.4%, PC2 9.7% var) -> Ward k=2 (50 vs 156, silhouette 0.472) -> all severity tests null (p >= 0.178 across 28 specifications).
grader_notes: The agent performed a rigorous and technically sound analysis; the only rubric deduction is for not applying a formal multiple-testing correction in criterion 5, while all other criteria meet the A-level standard.

Temporal dynamics of gene expression in rat vastus lateralis (SKM-VL) across 8 weeks of endurance training, and the sex-specific vs shared patterns (data: 766 training-regulated genes, MoTrPAC Nature 2024 supplementary table).

1) THE TIME COURSE IN EACH SEX
The number of genes with a significant expression change at each timepoint (timewise p < 0.05 vs sex-matched sedentary controls) grows with training duration in both sexes and is consistently larger in females:
- 1w: 145 genes (male) vs 220 (female), 33 shared
- 2w: 134 vs 329, 39 shared
- 4w: 176 vs 501, 107 shared
- 8w: 379 vs 532, 265 shared
Effect sizes are modest (median |log2FC| of significant genes 0.31-0.53) and up/down directions stay balanced (47-65% up) in both sexes. The male and female response profiles CONVERGE as training progresses: the correlation between male and female logFC vectors rises from r = 0.13 (1w) and 0.07 (2w) to r = 0.43 (4w) and 0.63 (8w), and among genes significant in both sexes the direction agreement rises from ~70% (1-2w) to ~99% (264/265 at 8w). Females mount a broader response at every timepoint (Fisher-combined p < 0.05 across the four timepoints: 614/766 females vs 379/766 males).

2) FIVE TEMPORAL ARCHETYPES (k-means on row-z-scored sex x timepoint logFC profiles; k=5; stable, mean ARI 0.997)
- C0 (n=153) - SHARED delayed-onset UP: flat at 1-2w, rises at 4-8w in both sexes. Overwhelmingly mitochondrial / oxidative phosphorylation genes (respiratory chain complex, aerobic respiration; g_SCS p < 1e-30). Examples: Ckmt2, Ckmt1, Atp6v1g2, Lgi3, Gpr88, Lamb3, mitochondrial Mt-co1/mt-Nd4l/Mt-atp8.
- C1 (n=203) - LATE REVERSAL UP / CONVERGENCE: males start negative (-0.28, -0.25 at 1-2w) and end strongly positive (+0.42 at 8w); females rise early and stay up. Enriched for angiogenesis and blood-vessel morphogenesis (p ~ 1e-6). Examples: Znf750, Hspb6, Apln (apelin), Fhl1, Ppm1e.
- C2 (n=104) - MALE-DOMINANT UP, females silent: male means +0.1 to +0.34 at all timepoints, female means slightly negative until 8w. Enriched for Z disc, myofibril, sarcomere. Examples: Ckmt1 (male +3.75 to +4.94, the strongest response in the dataset), sarcolipin Sln (male +2.44 at 8w vs female -1.54 at 2w), Iqgap2.
- C3 (n=79) - FEMALE-TRANSIENT UP / male down (most sex-divergent cluster, male-female profile correlation ~0.03): females spike at 1-2w (+0.40, +0.58) then return to baseline; males are negative throughout. Enriched for interstitial matrix, ECM structural constituent, fibrillar collagen. Examples: Tnmd (F +1.79 at 2w / M -2.46), Col11a1 (F +1.32 / M -2.00), Emilin3, plus proliferation markers Mki67, Prc1, Kif22, Iqgap3.
- C4 (n=227, largest) - SHARED PROGRESSIVE DOWN: both sexes drift to -0.23 to -0.26 by 8w. Enriched for endoplasmic/sarcoplasmic reticulum, carbohydrate catabolism, glycolytic process, muscle structure development. Examples: Bcat2, Prkag3 (AMPK gamma-3), Megf10, Adhfe1, Cpa1, Nmrk2, and Fos (AP-1 immediate-early, down in both sexes - resolution of the stress-response program).

3) SHARED VS SEX-SPECIFIC
The PREDOMINANT pattern is SHARED and biphasic: an early (1-2w) remodeling wave followed by a shared delayed build-up of oxidative-mitochondrial genes (C0) and shared progressive repression of ER/glycolytic/structural genes (C4); by 8w the sexes induce/repress largely the same genes (Jaccard 0.41, direction agreement 99%), differing mainly in breadth (532 vs 379 significant genes).
The genuinely SEX-SPECIFIC component is EARLY and TRANSIENT: direct male-vs-female contrast tests (Wald z on logFC differences, BH-corrected per timepoint) give 11 dimorphic genes at 1w and 47 at 2w, but ZERO at 4w and 8w. These early dimorphic genes are enriched for collagen/ECM terms (collagen trimer, collagen fibril assembly, p ~ 0.002-0.03) and are mostly stronger in FEMALES (Col11a1, Tnmd, Col8a2, Lox, Ltbp2, Meox1, Gdf11; a few male-higher: Tnfrsf12a, Slco4a1). A male-skewed myofibrillar program (C2) persists as a quantitative (not per-gene-significant) difference.
Corroborating non-transcript layers in SKM-VL: metabolomics mirrors the timeline (glutathione down ~-3.7 logFC at 8w in both sexes; acylcarnitines/lysophospholipids and 1-methylnicotinamide up), and immunoassay shows a female-skewed early VEGF/IL-6/MIP2/LIX response (VEGF up at all four female timepoints), consistent with the female early ECM/angiogenic archetype.

BOTTOM LINE: In SKM-VL, endurance training produces a small-magnitude (|log2FC| mostly < 0.5), bidirectional transcriptional remodeling that broadens steadily over 8 weeks. Females respond earlier and more broadly than males; the early female response is dominated by ECM/collagen, immune and angiogenic programs plus proliferation markers, while a male-biased myofibrillar/contractile program appears in parallel. From 4 weeks onward both sexes converge onto the same shared program - delayed induction of mitochondrial oxidative-phosphorylation genes and progressive repression of ER/glycolytic/structural genes - so by 8 weeks the response is predominantly SHARED in direction and identity, retaining only a quantitative female bias in the number of responsive genes. Formal statistical support for sex dimorphism (BH q < 0.05) is confined to the first two weeks.

Baseline circulating T cell populations that associate with 1-year overall survival in metastatic pancreatic cancer patients treated with nivolumab + chemotherapy (gem/nab-paclitaxel, PRINCE arm A1, n = 34 randomized, n = 25 with baseline CyTOF, n = 21 classifiable for 1-year OS plus 4 censored before day 365 retained in Cox models):

FAVORABLE DIRECTION (higher baseline frequency -> longer survival):
1. Tbet+ TCR-gamma-delta+ T cells (Tbet+ TCRgd+ T cells, % of TCRgd T cells; baseline median 0.79): strongest signal. Per-SD Cox HR 0.31 (95% CI 0.16-0.60, p = 0.0005; Holm-adjusted across 7 populations p = 0.0035). Kaplan-Meier median split: 1-year OS 0.89 (high) vs 0.42 (low), log-rank p = 0.0067. Also significant in a pooled 3-arm analysis with arm adjustment (HR 0.53, p = 0.006) and after Holm correction for the dichotomous endpoint (p = 0.024).
2. NKT cells (% of leukocytes; baseline median ~1.6e-2): per-SD odds ratio 5.56 for being alive at 1 year (logistic p = 0.025); per-SD Cox HR 0.48 (p = 0.008; Holm p = 0.050). Median split: 1-year OS 1.00 (high) vs 0.33 (low), log-rank p = 0.0017; 11 of 13 NKT-low patients died within 1 year.
3. Tbet+ T cells (% of CD3+ T cells; baseline median 0.18): per-SD Cox HR 0.54 (p = 0.033); median split 1-year OS 0.79 vs 0.50, log-rank p = 0.0075. Consistent but weaker in the pooled sensitivity analysis (HR 0.69, p = 0.042).

UNFAVORABLE DIRECTION (higher baseline frequency -> worse survival):
4. Ki-67+ cycling T cells (% of CD3+ T cells; baseline median 0.95, inverse marker): per-SD odds ratio 0.022 (logistic p = 0.050), per-SD Cox HR 2.28 (p = 0.044); median split 1-year OS 0.36 (high) vs 0.90 (low), log-rank p = 0.034. This signal was not reproduced in the pooled all-arms analysis (HR 1.27, p = 0.27) and is the least robust of the four.

NOT ASSOCIATED with 1-year OS in this cohort: HLA-DR+ non-naive (activated-memory) CD4 T cells, HLA-DR+ non-naive CD8 T cells, and total HLA-DR+ T cells (all Cox p >= 0.29; cross-validated AUCs 0.34-0.41). A prespecified multivariable model of the conventional activation axis (Tbet+ CD3+ plus HLA-DR+ CD4/CD8) was globally non-significant (LR p = 0.054, CV AUC 0.644).

KEY CONTEXT:
- The four signals form a single correlated immune axis (NKT vs Ki-67 Spearman rho = -0.91; NKT vs Tbet+ rho = 0.85), i.e., patients with a higher baseline innate-like, T-bet-expressing type-1 T cell compartment and a lower fraction of cycling peripheral T cells lived past 1 year on nivo/chemo. A post-hoc composite of NKT + Tbet+ gamma-delta + Ki-67 gave LR p = 0.002 with cross-validated out-of-fold AUC 0.779 (hypothesis-generating only, because the markers were selected on the same data).
- Associations are PROGNOSTIC, not proven predictive: no arm x marker interaction was detectable across the nivo/chemo, sotigalimab/chemo and triple-combination arms (all interaction p >= 0.088), so these populations likely track general host immune fitness in this chemo-immunotherapy setting.
- Limitations: single-arm focus within a small randomized phase-2 dataset (n = 21-25), 9/34 arm-A1 patients lacked baseline CyTOF and had shorter survival (median OS 303 vs 445 days, log-rank p = 0.12), 4 patients censored before day 365 were unclassifiable for the dichotomous endpoint, the deep T cell panel exists only at baseline (C1D1) so no kinetic biomarkers could be assessed, no external validation, and all inference is exploratory (Holm correction applied only within the prespecified 7-marker families). These markers require prospective validation before clinical use.

Question: Which genomic regions show reduced H3K27ac signal upon AI-10-49 treatment (candidate enhancers driving leukemia maintenance in inv(16) AML)?

ANSWER SUMMARY
AI-10-49 (CBFbeta-SMMHC inhibitor) treatment of ME-1 inv(16) AML cells causes a global collapse of H3K27ac at RUNX1/CBFbeta-SMMHC-dependent regulatory elements. Of 71,106 consensus H3K27ac regions tested (500 bp windows centered on union MACS2 summits from both conditions), 3,473 regions show a significant >=2-fold reduction in H3K27ac (log2FC(AI/DMSO) < -1, FDR < 0.05, edgeR exact test): 1,297 promoters and 2,175 distal enhancer candidates. Within the reduced set, H3K27ac fragments drop to ~0.31x of DMSO levels, versus 0.70x genome-wide. Reduced regions are significantly enriched for RUNX1 occupancy (distal: OR 2.25, p = 1.7e-07 vs RUNX1-DMSO peaks), while regions that GAIN acetylation are depleted of RUNX1 (OR 0.15, p = 2.1e-23), consistent with collapse of the fusion-factor enhancer program.

TOP REDUCED REGIONS (hg19/GRCh37 coordinates)

Distal enhancer candidates (strongest by FDR):
- chr3:14,798,820-14,799,319   nearest AC090957.2 (9.9 kb)   573->96 frags  log2FC -2.17  FDR 8.6e-13
- chr1:1,830,974-1,831,473     nearest RP1-140A9.1 (8.3 kb)  384->59 frags  log2FC -2.29  FDR 2.8e-12
- chr22:28,007,677-28,008,176  nearest RP1-231P7P.1 (38 kb)  275->37 frags  log2FC -2.48  FDR 4.0e-12
- chr22:20,146,138-20,146,637  nearest AC006547.14 (8.0 kb)  469->80 frags  log2FC -2.14  FDR 4.3e-12
- chr19:49,255,462-49,255,961  nearest FUT1 (2.9 kb)         294->43 frags  log2FC -2.36  FDR 1.3e-11
- chr20:31,215,124-31,215,623  nearest RP11-410N8.4 (40 kb)  216->27 frags  log2FC -2.59  FDR 2.3e-11  RUNX1-bound (DMSO and AI)
- chr16:85,411,619-85,412,118  nearest RP11-680G10.1 (21 kb) 261->43 frags  log2FC -2.19  FDR 8.1e-10  RUNX1-bound
- chr11:69,468,677-69,469,176  nearest CCND1 (13 kb)         545->116 frags log2FC -1.82  FDR 8.3e-10
- chr8:27,468,640-27,469,139   nearest CLU (3.7 kb)          365->69 frags  log2FC -1.99  FDR 6.9e-10

Leukemia-maintenance loci losing H3K27ac (therapeutically most relevant):
- MEIS1 locus (chr2:66.66-66.71 Mb), 2 distal regions: chr2:66,661,662-66,662,161 (211->49 frags, 0.23x, log2FC -1.70, FDR 3.5e-06) and chr2:66,704,122-66,704,621 (151->53, log2FC -1.10, FDR 4.9e-03). MEIS1 with HOXA9 is a core self-renewal/maintenance module in inv(16) AML.
- CCND1 distal enhancer (chr11:69,468,677-69,469,176): 545->116 frags (0.21x, FDR 8.3e-10); cyclin D1 cell-cycle driver.
- MN1 promoter/5' regions (chr22:41.77 Mb): 3 reduced regions, strongest 0.24x retention (log2FC -1.65, FDR 4.1e-07); MN1 is an adverse-prognostic oncogene in CN-AML.
- HOXA9 distal element (chr7, ~27.2 Mb region): 0.36x retention (log2FC -1.06, FDR 3.1e-04).
- FLT3 promoter (chr13:28.6 Mb): 0.36x retention (log2FC -1.05, FDR 1.3e-03), RUNX1-associated.
- MYC regulatory domain (chr8:128.75 Mb): strongest window decrease chr8:128,807,181-128,807,680 (136->50 frags, log2FC -1.03, FDR 0.011); promoter-proximal chr8:128,748,437-128,748,936 (471->226, FDR 0.037); window totals 1 reduced / 4 gained at FDR<0.05.

METHOD (one line each)
- Consensus regions: MACS2 summit points (narrowPeak col 10 offset) of H3K27ac peaks (FE>=2) from DMSO (GSM2715535; 57,818 summits) and AI-10-49 (GSM2715536; 56,298), clustered within 500 bp (bedtools merge -d 500) -> 71,107 clusters, expanded to 500 bp windows.
- Counting: bedtools multicov -q 30 on the two primary BAMs (35.95 M vs 37.33 M mapped reads).
- Statistics: edgeR exactTest (edgeR 4.0.16), TMM normalization, filterByExpr (71,106 kept); unreplicated design -> common dispersion fixed at phi = 0.01 (BCV = 0.1, isogenic clonal cell line per edgeR manual guidance); sensitivity sweep phi in {0.01, 0.04, 0.16, 0.25, 0.49} -> FDR<0.05 counts 13,950 / 532 / 0 / 0 / 0, so an effect-size floor (log2FC < -1) plus FDR < 0.05 defines the reduced set.
- Annotation: promoter = overlap with GENCODE v19 TSS +/- 2.5 kb; otherwise distal enhancer candidate; nearest gene by strand-aware TSS distance (bedtools closest); RUNX1 overlap vs merged peaks of GSM2715537 (DMSO, 1,329) and GSM2715538 (AI, 9,169); Fisher exact enrichment tests vs all-tested background.

CAVEATS
Single replicate per condition (p-values depend on the assumed BCV; fold-change ranks are robust); H3K27ac loss is treatment-responsive but not proof of causality; nearest-gene assignment for distal enhancers is heuristic (no 3D chromatin data); ATAC-seq/RNA-seq were not part of this workspace; RUNX1-DMSO peak set is sparse, so RUNX1 enrichment is conservative.

Full details: trace.md; tables: analysis/h3k27ac-differential/output/tables/

Interaction effect size between baseline insulin resistance status and the protein-vs-fiber preload contrast on rice peak glucose (mitigator challenge data, rice experiments):

PRIMARY ESTIMATE (subject-level, within-person):
- Interaction slope: +0.17 mg/dL peak glucose per SSPG unit (beta = +0.1697, 95% CI +0.031 to +0.308, p = 0.019, n = 19 subjects with SSPG).
- Standardized effect size: Pearson r = +0.53 (= standardized beta; bootstrap 95% CI +0.20 to +0.77; sign-flip permutation p = 0.006).

DERIVATION:
- For each of the 23 subjects who completed both rice pre-load arms, peak glucose = max CGM glucose (mg/dL) over 0-170 min, median-combined across replicates.
- delta_protein = Peak(Rice+Protein) - Peak(Rice) = -15.5 mg/dL (p = 0.005).
- delta_fiber   = Peak(Rice+Fiber) - Peak(Rice)   = -10.5 mg/dL (p = 0.089).
- Within-subject interaction contrast DID = delta_protein - delta_fiber, regressed on baseline SSPG (steady-state plasma glucose; higher = more insulin-resistant).

GROUP EFFECT SIZE (median SSPG split, 75 mg/L, of the 19 analytic subjects):
- Low-IR (n = 9):  DID = -18.35 mg/dL (protein pre-load blunts the rice peak ~18 mg/dL more than fiber).
- High-IR (n = 10): DID = +5.35 mg/dL (protein advantage abolished; fiber marginally lower peak).
- Difference = +23.7 mg/dL (95% CI +3.9 to +43.5, p = 0.022); Cohen's d = +1.16 (large).
- Using the cohort-wide SSPG median (107): difference = +21.5 mg/dL, p = 0.049, d = +1.01.

GROUP-LEVEL CONFIRMATION (linear mixed model, peak ~ arm x IR, random intercept per subject, all 31 SSPG-typed subjects, 132 replicate peaks):
- arm x IR interaction contrast [Protein:IR - Rice:IR] = +27.9 mg/dL (SE 10.9, z = 2.55, p = 0.011); +27.5 mg/dL (p = 0.010) restricted to the 23 dual-preload subjects.

SENSITIVITY:
- SSPG tertiles: mean DID -17.9 -> -8.1 -> +7.7 mg/dL (monotone with IR).
- Winsorizing peaks (5-95%): r = +0.537 (p = 0.018). Random-replicate peaks: r = +0.521.
- HOMA-IR instead of SSPG (n = 23): r = +0.16 (p = 0.46) - not significant.
- Incremental-AUC endpoint: r = +0.27 (p = 0.26) - same sign, not significant.
- Fat pre-load control (Rice+Fat vs Rice, same 19 subjects): r = +0.20 (p = 0.40) - the SSPG moderation is specific to the protein-vs-fiber contrast.

INTERPRETATION: Baseline insulin resistance moderates the mitigator effect - the peak-glucose reduction from a protein pre-load relative to a fiber pre-load shrinks by about 1.7 mg/dL for every +10 mg/L of SSPG (r = +0.53, d = 1.16 high- vs low-IR), crossing zero near SSPG ~ 140-150 mg/L. Protein pre-loading is the better mitigator only in insulin-sensitive individuals; in insulin-resistant individuals the two pre-loads are equivalent or fiber is modestly better.

CAVEATS: n = 19-31; SSPG missing for 4 of 23 dual-preload subjects; effect attenuates to non-significance under HOMA-IR or iAUC endpoints; dichotomization threshold changes the group difference (21.5-27.9 mg/dL range). Treat as hypothesis-generating.

Shared genetic factors among the 13 neonatal metabolites/ratios with GWAS summary statistics (266,162 trait-SNP rows = 20,474 common SNPs x 13 traits, discovery + replication cohorts):

PRIMARY SHARED GENETIC FACTOR — one pleiotropic locus at chr1:75,641,621-75,961,389 (GRCh38), inside the ACADM gene (medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase, MCAD), simultaneously influences FOUR carnitine-related traits:
  - C6 (hexanoylcarnitine), lead rs1250876 (1:75727547 A>G, intronic ACADM), beta = -0.0019 (-4.9% of mean/allele), p = 2.9e-13
  - C8 (octanoylcarnitine), lead rs2792082 (1:75736585 G>T, intronic ACADM), beta = -0.0027 (~-3%), p = 1.8e-10
  - C8/C2 (octanoylcarnitine/acetylcarnitine ratio), same rs1250876, p = 6.3e-10
  - (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 (malonyl+3-OH-isovalerylcarnitine/decenoylcarnitine ratio), lead rs1250877 (1:75727809 A>C, intronic ACADM), beta = +0.090 (+4.9%), p = 1.2e-12
Evidence that it is ONE shared factor, not four: the three lead SNPs are within 10 kb and in strong LD (1000G KHV r2 = 0.77-0.82, D' ~ 1); per-SNP effect directions across the locus are concordant between C6, C8 and C8/C2 (sign agreement 100%, beta correlation 0.995-0.999) and exactly inverted for the ratio trait (r = -0.995); 96-98% of the 275 discovery-significant SNP-trait rows at this locus replicate in the independent cohort (replication lead p = 1.9e-13, 8.9e-17, 2.4e-19 and 4.0e-12 respectively). Biologically coherent: ACADM performs the first beta-oxidation step of medium-chain (C4-C12) acyl-CoAs; alleles tagging lower MCAD activity raise medium-chain acylcarnitines (C6, C8, C8/C2) and shift (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 as expected from reduced beta-oxidation flux (the quantitative, common-variant counterpart of the MCAD-deficiency screening pattern of elevated C6/C8/C10).

SECONDARY (suggestive, NOT confirmed) SHARING — chr5:50,145,974-50,537,022 (EMB region; no closer protein-coding gene): C6DC (glutarylcarnitine) and C10:1 (decenoylcarnitine) share a perfectly correlated discovery signal (155 SNPs, beta r = 0.994, sign agreement 100%, 5 SNPs significant for both), but it FAILS replication (beta_rep ~ 0, p_rep = 0.94/0.91, Cochran Q = 28.5) and the replication cohort's C6DC signal maps to a different region (chr1:46.79-46.80 Mb near the CYP4B1/CYP4 family, p = 2.8e-10). Classified as cohort-heterogeneous, not a robust shared factor.

Broader shared structure (does not reach locus-sharing threshold): genome-wide genetic-effect correlations across all 20,474 SNPs show C6-C8 r = 0.805, C10:1-C8:1 r = 0.564, C10:1-C6DC r = 0.557, C4-C6 r = 0.531, plus C8-C6 phenotype correlation r = 0.737 (n = 8,674) - small polygenic sharing on top of the dominant ACADM locus.

Overall locus architecture (11 distinct loci from 592 genome-wide significant trait-SNP rows; 9/11 replicate): 1 four-trait pleiotropic locus (ACADM), 8 replicated single-trait loci that each land in a gene directly matching the metabolite's biochemistry, and 2 non-replicated loci (chr5 EMB-region C6DC/C10:1; chr15 SH2D7 C0). Gene-matched single-trait loci: C4 -> ACADS (rs34673751, p = 5.4e-25); C4DC+C5-OH -> CRAT (rs10988198, strongest signal in the dataset, p = 1.3e-63 discovery / 8.7e-92 replication); TYR -> HPD (rs2620332, p = 9.5e-34); PRO -> PRODH (rs4269009, p = 9.1e-42); C8:1 -> ACSM2A/ACSM2B (rs59261767, annotated stop_gained, p = 2.8e-12); C6DC -> CPT2 (rs76880674, p = 8.0e-10); C0 -> intergenic rs2510389 ~113 kb from CPT1A (p = 3.6e-20); C10:1 -> intergenic rs10890426, 9.2 kb from CYP4A11 (p = 1.8e-10). ORN/CIT had no genome-wide significant locus (min p = 4.3e-7).

Conclusion: the dominant shared genetic factor among these neonatal metabolites is the common ACADM (MCAD) haplotype on chr1:75.6 Mb that jointly determines hexanoylcarnitine (C6), octanoylcarnitine (C8), the C8/C2 ratio and the (C3DC+C4-OH)/C10 ratio, i.e. genetic variation in mitochondrial medium-chain fatty-acid beta-oxidation is the main point of genetic convergence across neonatal acylcarnitine traits; remaining single-trait loci map one-to-one onto the enzyme of the corresponding metabolite pathway (ACADS, CRAT, HPD, PRODH, ACSM2A, CPT2, CPT1A-proximal, CYP4A11-proximal), and the C6DC-C10:1 signal on chr5 is suggestive but fails replication.

Limitations: common-SNP panel only (20,474 SNPs, MAF >= 1.07%; rare pathogenic alleles invisible; leads are tagging variants, not proven causal); no individual-level genotypes (no conditional/fine-mapping/colocalization; locus definition used a 500 kb distance rule); one discovery cohort (chr5 locus shows cross-cohort heterogeneity); sample sizes not recoverable from the files (SE-implied N implausible); nearest-gene assignment for intergenic loci is a hypothesis.

GENOMIC LANDSCAPE OF BREAST CANCER RECEPTOR SUBTYPES
Cohort: MSK-IMPACT targeted-panel profiling, 1,803 samples from 1,649 patients (HR+/HER2- 1,422; HR+/HER2+ 141; HR-/HER2+ 66; TNBC 174), from data_clinical_sample.txt (1,918 samples; 115 excluded for unknown/equivocal receptor status), data_mutations.txt (9,314 MAF rows, 9,268 nonsynonymous) and data_cna.txt (474 genes; only deep-deletion -2 and amplification +2 calls present).

HOW THE LANDSCAPES DIFFER

1) TP53 defines a graded loss-of-function axis. Mutation frequency rises monotonically from HR+/HER2- 26.8% (381/1,422) to HR+/HER2+ 45.4% (64/141), HR-/HER2+ 78.8% (52/66) and TNBC 89.7% (156/174); overall association chi-square q = 5e-68. Truncating TP53 lesions are most frequent in TNBC (56% of mutated tumors vs 37% in HR+/HER2-). TP53 is the near-universal lesion of triple-negative and HER2-enriched disease.

2) PI3K-pathway alterations define HR+ disease and invert in TNBC. PIK3CA: 41.1% HR+/HER2-, 38.3% HR+/HER2+, 25.8% HR-/HER2+, 14.4% TNBC (OR = 0.24, TNBC vs HR+/HER2-, p = 4e-13; hotspots p.H1047R/L, p.E545K, p.E542K in all subtypes). PIK3R1 shows the opposite polarity (1.3% HR+/HER2- vs 7.5% TNBC, q = 1.7e-5), and AKT1 p.E17K is almost confined to HR+/HER2- (6.3%). PTEN inactivation (mutation or deep deletion) is most common in TNBC (14.9%; deep deletion OR = 3.1, p = 0.007). Any PI3K-pathway alteration: 54% HR+/HER2-, 45% HR+/HER2+, 33% HR-/HER2+ and TNBC.

3) GATA3 is a binary luminal marker: 17.5% (HR+/HER2-) and 17.0% (HR+/HER2+) vs 0 of 240 HR- tumors (Fisher p = 5.5e-19). Similarly MAP3K1 (9.0% HR+/HER2- vs 1.5-2.9% elsewhere), MAP2K4 (4.0%), AKT1 and the 11q13 (CCND1 21.1%, FGF19/FGF3/FGF4) and 8p11-12 (FGFR1 13.2%, PAK1 11.4%) amplifications mark HR+ (especially HR+/HER2-) tumors. CDH1 mutation (18.7% in HR+/HER2-) is histology-driven: 81% of lobular vs 2.0% of ductal HR+/HER2- tumors (OR = 210.6, p = 8e-169).

4) ERBB2/17q12 amplification is the genomic definition of the HER2+ arms: 66.7% of HR+/HER2+ and 86.4% of HR-/HER2+ samples vs 1.5% of HR+/HER2- and 0.6% of TNBC (OR 40.1 and 88.5, q = 2.6e-236). CDK12 is co-amplified with ERBB2 in 117/117 cases; RARA (19.1%), SPOP (13.5%) and HOXB13 amps tag the same 17q amplicon. Notably 1.5% of clinically HR+/HER2- tumors harbor ERBB2 amplification and 4.4% carry ERBB2 mutations - ERBB2-actionable subcohorts within receptor-negative-by-IHC disease. HER2+ tumors are also amplification-rich overall (mean 0.9-1.0% of panel genes amplified vs 0.5-0.6% in HR+/HER2-/TNBC, KW p = 1.4e-18) and more TP53-mutant.

5) TNBC has a distinct DNA-repair and amplicon profile: RB1 inactivation (mutation or deep deletion) 16.1% (deep deletion OR = 9.9, q = 2.3e-8), BRCA1/2 or PALB2 mutation 8.6% and any homologous-repair gene mutation 11.5% (the PARP-inhibitor subcohort), MYC amplification 15.5%, plus TNBC-restricted focal amplicons CCND2 (12p13, OR = 78.5), KDM5A, RAD52 and CCNE1 (19q12, 5.7%; all 10 CCNE1-amplified TNBC are TP53-mutant). MAP2K4 deep deletions, by contrast, are restricted to HR+ tumors (2.1%).

6) ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutations (Y537S/C/N, D538G - 130 of 175 ESR1 mutations) occur only in HR+ tumors (8.5-9.9%) and are 11-fold enriched in metastases vs treatment-naive primaries (15.0% vs 1.6%, OR = 11.1, p = 6e-23) - the genomic signature of endocrine-therapy exposure and acquired resistance. ESR1-mutant tumors are TP53-wild-type-enriched (OR = 0.39), marking a lower-grade luminal subgroup.

7) Mutation burden is low in all groups (median 3-4 nonsynonymous mutations/sample on the ~1.1 Mb panel; the provided TMB column is mis-scaled by a factor of 30 - counts/30 - and was recomputed). Medians: HR+/HER2- 3, HR+/HER2+ 3, HR-/HER2+ 4, TNBC 4; the overall difference is not significant (Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.085) and pairwise differences (TNBC and HR+/HER2+ vs HR+/HER2-, p = 0.014/0.042 unadjusted) do not survive correction - burden differences across subtypes are modest within this panel; the sole hypermutant (445 mutations) is an MSH2/MSH6/POLD1/POLE-mutant outlier.

ACTIONABLE SUBCOHORTS WITHIN RECEPTOR GROUPS (frequencies)
- PIK3CA mutation (alpelisib + endocrine): 41.1% HR+/HER2-, 38.3% HR+/HER2+, 25.8% HR-/HER2+, 14.4% TNBC.
- ERBB2 amplification (HER2-directed therapy): 86.4% HR-/HER2+, 66.7% HR+/HER2+, 1.5% HR+/HER2-, 0.6% TNBC; 21-22% of HER2+ tumors are also PIK3CA-mutant (co-targeting decisions).
- ESR1 mutation (elacestrant): ~8.5-9.9% of HR+ tumors (15% of HR+ metastases), 0% HR-.
- BRCA1/2/PALB2 (PARP inhibitors): 4.9-8.6% across subtypes, highest in TNBC (8.6%); any HRR-gene mutation 6-12%.
- PTEN loss (AKT inhibition): highest in TNBC (14.9%).
- CDK4/6-axis amplification (CCND1 or FGFR1): 29.2% HR+/HER2-, 26.2% HR+/HER2+, 12.1% HR-/HER2+, 8.0% TNBC.

BOTTOM LINE: HR+ tumors are PI3K/GATA3/ER-axis and 11q13/8p11 amplification driven with lobular CDH1 lesions and acquired ESR1-LBD mutations after endocrine therapy; HER2+ tumors (either HR background) are defined by 17q12 (ERBB2/CDK12) amplification on a TP53-mutant, amplification-rich background; TNBC is defined by near-universal TP53 loss-of-function plus RB1/PTEN inactivation, MYC/CCNE1/CCND2 amplification, and the highest homologous-repair-lesion load. Clinically, receptor status and genotype are complementary: every receptor group contains actionable subcohorts, most notably ERBB2 amplification in 1.5% of HR+/HER2- tumors, PIK3CA mutations in 14% of TNBC, and HRR lesions in 9-12% of every subtype.

LIMITATIONS: cross-sectional design (no treatment-response or survival data; "acquired" ESR1 inference rests on naive-primary vs metastatic comparison); targeted panel (no genome-wide CNA, signatures, or structural variants; gene-level +/-2 calls only, so amplicon membership is inferred); somatic variants only (germline BRCA1/2 carriers undercounted, so HRR fractions are lower bounds); small HR-/HER2+ arm (n = 66) gives low power; several small-gene signals (RHOA, PRDM1, PTPN11, CD79A, TGFBR1) are nominal; 154 patients contribute >1 sample; 6.8% of samples show primary-vs-sequenced-sample receptor discordance, blurring subtype boundaries.

Method summary: subtypes from RECEPTOR_STATUS_PRIMARY; nonsynonymous MAF rows collapsed to a binary gene-by-sample matrix (446 genes x 1,803 samples); CNA +/-2 calls aligned to the same samples; 4-group chi-square per gene with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, pairwise Fisher exact with odds ratios; Kruskal-Wallis/Mann-Whitney for burden; full trace with code in trace.md; tables in analysis/, figures in figures/.
